_comment: A web app on a single VPS with nginx and systemd. The recurring theme here is that one box serves several sites, so a mistake aimed at one of them takes down all of them. Copy to your project root as .blastradius.json and gitignore it.

rules.why: One nginx instance fronts every site on this box, not just this project. A bad config takes them all down together. Run nginx -t first.
This is the atomic swap that makes a release live. Confirm the target directory is the build you actually tested, because the swap itself is instant and silent.
Deleting inside the webroot. If it hits the live release rather than an old one, the site is down until you can rebuild and redeploy.
TLS private key material. Copying it off the box is an incident; deleting it takes HTTPS down for every site using it.
Schema migrations are frequently one-way. Take a dump first and confirm which database the connection string actually points at.
A deploy wrapper hides what it runs. blastradius reads local scripts where it can, but confirm you know which environment this one targets.
